1.text: Tha words of tha Preacher, tha son of David, king in Jerusalem.
Vanity of vanities, says tha Preacher, vanity of vanities; all is vanity.
What profit has a man of all his labour which he takes under tha sun?
One generation passes away, N another generation comes: but tha earth abides 4 ever.
Tha sun also arises, N tha sun goes down, N hurries 2 his place where he arose.
Tha wind goes toward tha south, N turns about 2 tha north; it whirleth about continually, N tha wind returns again according 2 his circuits.
All tha rivers run in2 tha sea; yet tha sea is not full; 2 tha place from from where tha rivers come, there dey return again.
All things r full of labour; man cannot utter it: tha eye is not satisfied wit seein, nor tha ear filled wit hearin.
Tha thing dat has been, it is dat which shall be; N dat which is done is dat which shall be done: N there is no new thing under tha sun.
Is there any thing whereof it may be said, See, dis is new? it has been already of old time, which was before us.
There is no remembrance of former things; neither shall there be any remembrance of things dat r 2 come wit dose dat shall come after.
I tha Preacher was king over Israel in Jerusalem.
N I gave my heart 2 seek N search out by wisdom concerning all things dat r done under heaven: dis sore travail has God given 2 tha sons of man 2 be exercised wit it.
I have seen all tha works dat r done under tha sun; N, look, all is vanity N vexation of spirit.
Dat which is crooked cannot be made straight: N dat which is wantin cannot be numbered.

I communed wit my own heart, sayin, look, I am come 2 great estate, N have got more wisdom than all dey dat have been before me in Jerusalem: yeah, my heart had great experience of wisdom N knowledge.
N I gave my heart 2 know wisdom, N 2 know madness N folly: I perceived dat dis also is vexation of spirit.
4 in much wisdom is much grief: N he dat increases knowledge increases sorrow.

2.text: I said in mine heart, Go 2 now, I will prove u wit mirth, therefore enjoy pleasure: N, look, dis also is vanity.
I said of laughter, It is mad: N of mirth, What does it?

I sought in mine heart 2 give myself 2 wine, yet acquainting mine heart wit wisdom; N 2 lay hold on folly, till I might see what was dat good 4 tha sons of men, which dey should do under tha heaven all tha days of their life.
I made me great works; I builded me houses; I planted me vineyards:
I made me gardens N orchards, N I planted trees in ’em of all kind of fruits:
I made me pools of water, 2 water wit it tha wood dat brings forth trees:
I got me servants N maidens, N had servants born in my house; also I had great possessions of great N small cattle above all dat were in Jerusalem before me:

I gathered me also silver N gold, N tha peculiar treasure of kings N of tha provinces: I got me men singers N women singers, N tha delights of tha sons of men, as musical instruments, N dat of all sorts.
So I was great, N increased more than all dat were before me in Jerusalem: also my wisdom remained wit me.
N whatever my eyes desired I kept not from ’em, I withheld not my heart from any joy; 4 my heart rejoiced in all my labour: N dis was my portion of all my labour.
Then I looked on all tha works dat my hands had wrought, N on tha labour dat I had laboured 2 do: N, look, all was vanity N vexation of spirit, N there was no profit under tha sun.
N I turned myself 2 look wisdom, N madness, N folly: 4 what can tha man do dat comes after tha king? even dat which has been already done.
Then I saw dat wisdom excelleth folly, as far as light excelleth darkness.
Tha wise man’s eyes r in his head; but tha fool walks in darkness: N I myself perceived also dat one event happens 2 ’em all.
Then said I in my heart, As it happens 2 tha fool, so it happens even 2 me; N why was I then more wise? Then I said in my heart, dat dis also is vanity.
4 there is no remembrance of tha wise more than of tha fool 4 ever; seein dat which now is in tha days 2 come shall all be forgotten. N how dies tha wise man? as tha fool.
Therefore I hated life; because tha work dat is wrought under tha sun is grievous 2 me: 4 all is vanity N vexation of spirit.
Yeah, I hated all my labour which I had taken under tha sun: because I should leave it 2 tha man dat shall be after me.
N who knows whether he shall be a wise man or a fool? yet shall he have rule over all my labour in which I have laboured, N in which I have showed myself wise under tha sun. dis is also vanity.
Therefore I went about 2 cause my heart 2 despair of all tha labour which I took under tha sun.
4 there is a man whose labour is in wisdom, N in knowledge, N in equity; yet 2 a man dat has not laboured in it shall he leave it 4 his portion. dis also is vanity N a great evil.
4 what has man of all his labour, N of tha vexation of his heart, in which he has laboured under tha sun?
4 all his days r sorrows, N his travail grief; yeah, his heart takes not rest in tha night. dis is also vanity.
There is nothing better 4 a man, than dat he should eat N drink, N dat he should make his soul enjoy good in his labour. dis also I saw, dat it was from tha hand of God.
4 who can eat, or who else can hasten hereunto, more than I?

4 God gives 2 a man dat is good in his sight wisdom, N knowledge, N joy: but 2 tha sinner he gives travail, 2 gather N 2 heap up, dat he may give 2 him dat is good before God. dis also is vanity N vexation of spirit.

3.text: 2 every thing there is a season, N a time 2 every purpose under tha heaven:
A time 2 be born, N a time 2 die; a time 2 plant, N a time 2 pluck up dat which is planted;
A time 2 kill, N a time 2 heal; a time 2 break down, N a time 2 build up;
A time 2 weep, N a time 2 laugh; a time 2 mourn, N a time 2 dance;
A time 2 cast away stones, N a time 2 gather stones together; a time 2 embrace, N a time 2 refrain from embracing;
A time 2 get, N a time 2 lose; a time 2 keep, N a time 2 cast away;
A time 2 rend, N a time 2 sew; a time 2 keep silence, N a time 2 speak;
A time 2 love, N a time 2 hate; a time of war, N a time of peace.
What profit has he dat works in dat in which he laboureth?
I have seen tha travail, which God has given 2 tha sons of men 2 be exercised in it.
He has made every thing beautiful in his time: also he has set tha world in their heart, so dat no man can find out tha work dat God makes from tha beginning 2 tha end.
I know dat there is no good in ’em, but 4 a man 2 rejoice, N 2 do good in his life.
N also dat every man should eat N drink, N enjoy tha good of all his labour, it is tha gift of God.
I know dat, whatever God does, it shall be 4 ever: nothing can be put 2 it, nor any thing taken from it: N God does it, dat men should fear before him.
Dat which has been is now; N dat which is 2 be has already been; N God requireth dat which is past.
N moreover I saw under tha sun tha place of judgment, dat wickedness was there; N tha place of righteousness, dat iniquity was there.
I said in mine heart, God shall judge tha righteous N tha wicked: 4 there is a time there 4 every purpose N 4 every work.
I said in mine heart concerning tha estate of tha sons of men, dat God might manifest ’em, N dat dey might see dat dey themselves r beasts.

4 dat which befalleth tha sons of men befalleth beasts; even one thing befalleth ’em: as tha one dies, so dies tha other; yeah, dey have all one breath; so dat a man has no preeminence above a beast: 4 all is vanity.
All go 2 one place; all r of tha dust, N all turn 2 dust again.
Who knows tha spirit of man dat goes upward, N tha spirit of tha beast dat goes downward 2 tha earth?
So I perceive dat there is nothing better, than dat a man should rejoice in his own works; 4 dat is his portion: 4 who shall bring him 2 see what shall be after him?

4.text: So I returned, N considered all tha oppressions dat r done under tha sun: N look tha tears of such as were oppressed, N dey had no comforter; N on tha side of their oppressors there was power; but dey had no comforter.
So I praised tha dead which r already dead more than tha livin which r yet alive.
Yeah, better is he than both dey, which has not yet been, who has not seen tha evil work dat is done under tha sun.
Again, I considered all travail, N every right work, dat 4 dis a man is envied of his neighbour. dis is also vanity N vexation of spirit.
Tha fool foldeth his hands together, N eats his own flesh.
Better is an handful wit quietness, than both tha hands full wit travail N vexation of spirit.
Then I returned, N I saw vanity under tha sun.

There is one alone, N there is not a second; yeah, he has neither child nor brother: yet is there no end of all his labour; neither is his eye satisfied wit riches; neither says he, 4 whom do I labour, N bereave my soul of good? dis is also vanity, yeah, it is a sore travail.
Two r better than one; because dey have a good reward 4 their labour.
4 if dey fall, tha one will lift up his fellow: but woe 2 him dat is alone when he falls; 4 he has not another 2 help him up.
Again, if two lie together, then dey have heat: but how can one be warm alone?
N if one prevail against him, two shall withstand him; N a threefold cord is not quickly broken.
Better is a poor N a wise child than an old N foolish king, who will no more be admonished.
4 out of prison he comes 2 reign; whereas also he dat is born in his kingdom becomes poor.
I considered all tha livin which walk under tha sun, wit tha second child dat shall stand up in his stead.
There is no end of all tha people, even of all dat have been before ’em: dey also dat come after shall not rejoice in him. Surely dis also is vanity N vexation of spirit.

5.text: Keep ur foot when u go 2 tha house of God, N be more ready 2 hear, than 2 give tha sacrifice of fools: 4 dey consider not dat dey do evil.
Don’t be rash wit ur mouth, N don’t let thine heart be hasty 2 utter any thing before God: 4 God is in heaven, N u upon earth: therefore let ur words be few.
4 a dream comes through tha crowd of business; N a fool’s voice is known by crowd of words.
When u vowest a vow 2 God, defer not 2 pay it; 4 he has no pleasure in fools: pay dat which u have vowed.
Better is it dat u should not vow, than dat u should vow N not pay.
Suffer not ur mouth 2 cause ur flesh 2 sin; neither say u before tha angel, dat it was an error: so should God be angry at ur voice, N destroy tha work of thine hands?
4 in tha crowd of dreams N many words there r also divers vanities: but fear u God.
If u see tha oppression of tha poor, N violent perverting of judgment N justice in a province, marvel not at tha matter: 4 he dat is higher than tha highest regards; N there be higher than dey.
Moreover tha profit of tha earth is 4 all: tha king himself is served by tha field.
He dat loves silver shall not be satisfied wit silver; nor he dat loves abundance wit increase: dis is also vanity.
When goods increase, dey r increased dat eat ’em: N what good is there 2 tha owners of it, saving tha beholding of ’em wit their eyes?
Tha sleep of a labouring man is sweet, whether he eat little or much: but tha abundance of tha rich will not suffer him 2 sleep.
There is a sore evil which I have seen under tha sun, namely, riches kept 4 tha owners of it 2 their hurt.
But dose riches perish by evil travail: N he begetteth a son, N there is nothing in his hand.
As he came forth of his mother’s womb, naked shall he return 2 go as he came, N shall take nothing of his labour, which he may carry away in his hand.
N dis also is a sore evil, dat in all points as he came, so shall he go: N what profit has he dat has laboured 4 tha wind?
All his days also he eats in darkness, N he has much sorrow N wrath wit his sickness.

Look dat which I have seen: it is good N comely 4 one 2 eat N 2 drink, N 2 enjoy tha good of all his labour dat he takes under tha sun all tha days of his life, which God gives him: 4 it is his portion.
Every man also 2 whom God has given riches N wealth, N has given him power 2 eat of it, N 2 take his portion, N 2 rejoice in his labour; dis is tha gift of God.
4 he shall not much remember tha days of his life; because God answers him in tha joy of his heart.

6.text: There is an evil which I have seen under tha sun, N it is common among men:

A man 2 whom God has given riches, wealth, N honour, so dat he wants nothing 4 his soul of all dat he desires, yet God gives him not power 2 eat of it, but a stranger eats it: dis is vanity, N it is an evil disease.

If a man beget an hundred children, N live many years, so dat tha days of his years be many, N his soul don’t be filled wit good, N also dat he have no burial; I say, dat an untimely birth is better than he.
4 he comes in wit vanity, N departs in darkness, N his name shall be covered wit darkness.
Moreover he has not seen tha sun, nor known any thing: dis has more rest than tha other.
Yeah, though he live a thousand years twice told, yet has he seen no good: do not all go 2 one place?
All tha labour of man is 4 his mouth, N yet tha appetite is not filled.
4 what has tha wise more than tha fool? what has tha poor, dat knows 2 walk before tha livin?
Better is tha sight of tha eyes than tha wandering of tha desire: dis is also vanity N vexation of spirit.
Dat which has been is named already, N it is known dat it is man: neither may he contend wit him dat is mightier than he.
Seein there be many things dat increase vanity, what is man tha better?
4 who knows what is good 4 man in dis life, all tha days of his vain life which he spendeth as a shadow? 4 who can tell a man what shall be after him under tha sun?

7.text: A good name is better than precious ointment; N tha day of death than tha day of one’s birth.
It is better 2 go 2 tha house of mournin, than 2 go 2 tha house of feasting: 4 dat is tha end of all men; N tha livin will lay it 2 his heart.
Sorrow is better than laughter: 4 by tha sadness of tha countenance tha heart is made better.
Tha heart of tha wise is in tha house of mournin; but tha heart of fools is in tha house of mirth.
It is better 2 hear tha rebuke of tha wise, than 4 a man 2 hear tha song of fools.
4 as tha crackling of thorns under a pot, so is tha laughter of tha fool: dis also is vanity.
Surely oppression makes a wise man mad; N a gift destroys tha heart.
Better is tha end of a thing than tha beginning of it: N tha patient in spirit is better than tha proud in spirit.
Don’t be hasty in ur spirit 2 be angry: 4 anger resteth in tha bosom of fools.
Say not u, What is tha cause dat tha former days were better than dese? 4 u do not enquire wisely concerning dis.
Wisdom is good wit an inheritance: N by it there is profit 2 ’em dat see tha sun.
4 wisdom is a defence, N money is a defence: but tha excellency of knowledge is, dat wisdom gives life 2 ’em dat have it.
Consider tha work of God: 4 who can make dat straight, which he has made crooked?
In tha day of prosperity be joyful, but in tha day of adversity consider: God also has set tha one over against tha other, 2 tha end dat man should find nothing after him.
All things have I seen in tha days of my vanity: there is a just man dat perishes in his righteousness, N there is a wicked man dat prolongeth his life in his wickedness.
Don’t be righteous over much; neither make urself over wise: why should u destroy urself?
Don’t be over much wicked, neither be u foolish: why should u die before ur time?
It is good dat u should take hold of dis; yeah, also from dis withdraw not thine hand: 4 he dat fears God shall come forth of ’em all.
Wisdom strengthens tha wise more than ten mighty men which r in tha city.
4 there is not a just man upon earth, dat does good, N sins not.
Also take no heed 2 all words dat r spoken; lest u hear ur servant curse u:
4 oftentimes also ur own heart knows dat u urself likewise have cursed others.
All dis have I proved by wisdom: I said, I will be wise; but it was far from me.
Dat which is far off, N exceeding deep, who can find it out?
I applied mine heart 2 know, N 2 search, N 2 seek out wisdom, N tha reason of things, N 2 know tha wickedness of folly, even of foolishness N madness:
N I find more bitter than death tha woman, whose heart is snares N nets, N her hands as bands: whoever pleaseth God shall escape from her; but tha sinner shall be taken by her.
Look, dis have I found, says tha preacher, counting one by one, 2 find out tha account:
Which yet my soul seeks, but I find not: one man among a thousand have I found; but a woman among all dose have I not found.
Look, dis only have I found, dat God has made man upright; but dey have sought out many inventions.

8.text: Who is as tha wise man? N who knows tha interpretation of a thing? a man’s wisdom makes his face 2 shine, N tha boldness of his face shall be changed.
I counsel u 2 keep tha king’s commandment, N dat in regard of tha oath of God.
Don’t be hasty 2 go out of his sight: stand not in an evil thing; 4 he does whatever pleaseth him.
Where tha word of a king is, there is power: N who may say 2 him, What do u?
Whoever keeps tha commandment shall feel no evil thing: N a wise man’s heart discerneth both time N judgment.
Because 2 every purpose there is time N judgment, therefore tha misery of man is great upon him.
4 he knows not dat which shall be: 4 who can tell him when it shall be?

There is no man dat has power over tha spirit 2 retain tha spirit; neither has he power in tha day of death: N there is no discharge in dat war; neither shall wickedness deliver dose dat r given 2 it.
All dis have I seen, N applied my heart 2 every work dat is done under tha sun: there is a time in which one man rules over another 2 his own hurt.
N so I saw tha wicked buried, who had come N gone from tha place of tha holy, N dey were forgotten in tha city where dey had so done: dis is also vanity.
Because sentence against an evil work is not executed speedily, therefore tha heart of tha sons of men is fully set in ’em 2 do evil.
Though a sinner do evil an hundred times, N his days be prolonged, yet surely I know dat it shall be well wit ’em dat fear God, which fear before him:
But it shall not be well wit tha wicked, neither shall he prolong his days, which r as a shadow; because he fears not before God.

There is a vanity which is done upon tha earth; dat there be just men, 2 whom it happens according 2 tha work of tha wicked; again, there be wicked men, 2 whom it happens according 2 tha work of tha righteous: I said dat dis also is vanity.

Then I commended mirth, because a man has no better thing under tha sun, than 2 eat, N 2 drink, N 2 be merry: 4 dat shall abide wit him of his labour tha days of his life, which God gives him under tha sun.
When I applied mine heart 2 know wisdom, N 2 see tha business dat is done upon tha earth: (4 also there is dat neither day nor night sees sleep wit his eyes:)

Then I beheld all tha work of God, dat a man cannot find out tha work dat is done under tha sun: because though a man labour 2 seek it out, yet he shall not find it; yeah further; though a wise man think 2 know it, yet shall he not be able 2 find it.

9.text: 4 all dis I considered in my heart even 2 declare all dis, dat tha righteous, N tha wise, N their works, r in tha hand of God: no man knows either love or hatred by all dat is before ’em.

All things come alike 2 all: there is one event 2 tha righteous, N 2 tha wicked; 2 tha good N 2 tha clean, N 2 tha unclean; 2 him dat sacrificeth, N 2 him dat sacrificeth not: as is tha good, so is tha sinner; N he dat swears, as he dat fears an oath.

Dis is an evil among all things dat r done under tha sun, dat there is one event 2 all: yeah, also tha heart of tha sons of men is full of evil, N madness is in their heart while dey live, N after dat dey go 2 tha dead.
4 2 him dat is joined 2 all tha livin there is hope: 4 a livin dog is better than a dead lion.
4 tha livin know dat dey shall die: but tha dead know not any thing, neither have dey any more a reward; 4 tha memory of ’em is forgotten.
Also their love, N their hatred, N their envy, is now perished; neither have dey any more a portion 4 ever in any thing dat is done under tha sun.
Go ur way, eat ur bread wit joy, N drink ur wine wit a merry heart; 4 God now accepteth ur works.
Let ur garments be always white; N let ur head lack no ointment.

Live joyfully wit tha wife whom u love all tha days of tha life of ur vanity, which he has given u under tha sun, all tha days of ur vanity: 4 dat is ur portion in dis life, N in ur labour which u take under tha sun.
Whatever ur hand finds 2 do, do it wit ur might; 4 there is no work, nor device, nor knowledge, nor wisdom, in tha grave, where u go.

I returned, N saw under tha sun, dat tha race is not 2 tha swift, nor tha battle 2 tha strong, neither yet bread 2 tha wise, nor yet riches 2 men of understanding, nor yet favour 2 men of skill; but time N chance happens 2 ’em all.
4 man also knows not his time: as tha fishes dat r taken in an evil net, N as tha birds dat r caught in tha snare; so r tha sons of men snared in an evil time, when it falls suddenly upon ’em.
Dis wisdom have I seen also under tha sun, N it seemed great 2 me:
There was a little city, N few men within it; N there came a great king against it, N besieged it, N built great bulwarks against it:
Now there was found in it a poor wise man, N he by his wisdom delivered tha city; yet no man remembered dat same poor man.
Then said I, Wisdom is better than strength: nevertheless tha poor man’s wisdom is despised, N his words r not heard.
Tha words of wise men r heard in quiet more than tha cry of him dat rules among fools.
Wisdom is better than weapons of war: but one sinner destroys much good.

10.text: Dead flies cause tha ointment of tha apothecary 2 send forth a stinking savour: so does a little folly him dat is in reputation 4 wisdom N honour.
A wise man’s heart is at his right hand; but a fool’s heart at his left.
Yeah also, when he dat is a fool walks by tha way, his wisdom fails him, N he says 2 every one dat he is a fool.
If tha spirit of tha ruler rise up against u, leave not ur place; 4 yielding pacifieth great offences.
There is an evil which I have seen under tha sun, as an error which proceeds from tha ruler:
Folly is set in great dignity, N tha rich sit in low place.
I have seen servants upon horses, N princes walkin as servants upon tha earth.
He dat diggeth a pit shall fall in2 it; N whoever breaks an hedge, a serpent shall bite him.
Whoever removeth stones shall be hurt wit it; N he dat clings wood shall be endangered by dat.
If tha iron be blunt, N he do not whet tha edge, then must he put 2 more strength: but wisdom is profitable 2 direct.
Surely tha serpent will bite without enchantment; N a babbler is no better.
Tha words of a wise man’s mouth r gracious; but tha lips of a fool will swallow up himself.
Tha beginning of tha words of his mouth is foolishness: N tha end of his talk is mischievous madness.
A fool also is full of words: a man cannot tell what shall be; N what shall be after him, who can tell him?
Tha labour of tha foolish wearieth every one of ’em, because he knows not how 2 go 2 tha city.
Woe 2 u, O land, when ur king is a child, N ur princes eat in tha morning!
Blessed r u, O land, when ur king is tha son of nobles, N ur princes eat in due season, 4 strength, N not 4 drunkenness!
By much slothfulness tha buildin decayeth; N through idleness of tha hands tha house droppeth through.
A feast is made 4 laughter, N wine makes merry: but money answers all things.
Curse not tha king, no not in ur thought; N curse not tha rich in ur bedchamber: 4 a bird of tha air shall carry tha voice, N dat which has wings shall tell tha matter.

11.text: Cast ur bread upon tha waterz: 4 u will find it after many days.
Give a portion 2 seven, N also 2 eight; 4 u know not what evil shall be upon tha earth.
If tha clouds be full of rain, dey empty themselves upon tha earth: N if tha tree fall toward tha south, or toward tha north, in tha place where tha tree falls, there it shall be.
He dat observeth tha wind shall not sow; N he dat regards tha clouds shall not reap.
As u know not what is tha way of tha spirit, nor how tha bones do grow in tha womb of her dat is wit child: even so u know not tha works of God who makes all.
In tha morning sow ur seed, N in tha evening withhold not thine hand: 4 u know not whether shall prosper, either dis or dat, or whether dey both shall be alike good.
Truly tha light is sweet, N a pleasant thing it is 4 tha eyes 2 look tha sun:
But if a man live many years, N rejoice in ’em all; yet let him remember tha days of darkness; 4 dey shall be many. All dat comes is vanity.

Rejoice, O young man, in ur youth; N let ur heart cheer u in tha days of ur youth, N walk in tha ways of thine heart, N in tha sight of ur eyes: but know u, dat 4 all dese things God will bring u in2 judgment.
Therefore remove sorrow from ur heart, N put away evil from ur flesh: 4 childhood N youth r vanity.

12.text: Remember now ur Creator in tha days of ur youth, while tha evil days come not, nor tha years draw nigh, when u will say, I have no pleasure in ’em;
While tha sun, or tha light, or tha moon, or tha stars, don’t be darkened, nor tha clouds return after tha rain:
In tha day when tha keepers of tha house shall tremble, N tha strong men shall bow themselves, N tha grinders cease because dey r few, N dose dat look out of tha windows be darkened,
N tha doors shall be shut in tha streets, when tha sound of tha grinding is low, N he shall rise up at tha voice of tha bird, N all tha daughters of musick shall be brought low;

Also when dey shall be afraid of dat which is high, N fears shall be in tha way, N tha almond tree shall flourish, N tha grasshopper shall be a burden, N desire shall fail: because man goes 2 his long home, N tha mourners go about tha streets:
Or ever tha silver cord be loosed, or tha golden bowl be broken, or tha pitcher be broken at tha fountain, or tha wheel broken at tha cistern.
Then shall tha dust return 2 tha earth as it was: N tha spirit shall return 2 God who gave it.
Vanity of vanities, says tha preacher; all is vanity.
N moreover, because tha preacher was wise, he still taught tha people knowledge; yeah, he gave good heed, N sought out, N set in order many proverbs.
Tha preacher sought 2 find out acceptable words: N dat which was written was upright, even words of truth.
Tha words of tha wise r as goads, N as nails fastened by tha masters of assemblies, which r given from one shepherd.
N further, by dese, my son, be admonished: of makin many books there is no end; N much study is a weariness of tha flesh.
Let us hear tha conclusion of tha whole matter: Fear God, N keep his commandments: 4 dis is tha whole duty of man.
4 God shall bring every work in2 judgment, wit every secret thing, whether it be good, or whether it be evil.
